title: Buildrathon Kickoff: Code the Future with CMC Global
content:
On September 26, 2026, I attended Buildrathon Kickoff: Code the Future with CMC Global at Bitexco Financial Tower. As a Software Engineering student interning in the First Cloud AI Journey program, I saw this as an opportunity to explore Cloud and AI, hear from industry practitioners, and find direction for my AWS learning.
Event information Scheduled time — 9:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m., Saturday, September 26, 2026 (UTC+7). Location — AWS Vietnam office, Bitexco Financial Tower, 2 Hai Trieu Street, Sai Gon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City. Role — Attendee. Talkshow topic displayed at the event — The Thinking Behind Building the Bot. The event page provides the introduction and registration information. Buildrathon Kickoff on Luma My objectives I wanted to learn more about Buildrathon and connect what I was studying with a practical problem. My interests included
Understanding the program’s direction and how to prepare for a product-building challenge. Hearing industry perspectives on Cloud, AI, and career development. Finding ideas for further study and a practical project during my internship. Getting to know the AWS community and other students with similar interests. Speaker and session topics The event standee identified Bùi Nhật Trường, Technical Leader at CMC Global, as the speaker for The Thinking Behind Building the Bot. The topic prompted me to think about the preparation behind an AI application, from understanding a need to organizing how a system handles requests.
Introducing Buildrathon The opening introduced the program and provided context for learning and building with Cloud and AI. I connected this introduction with my own AWS studies. A service becomes easier to understand when I can explain the problem it solves and where it fits within a system.
One practice I want to adopt is defining a clear outcome before starting an exercise. For a small project, I should be able to explain who will use it, which functionality they need, and how I will check that it works.
Thinking through an AI application The talkshow topic drew my attention to the design decisions behind a product. For a user-facing bot, I want to explore how requests arrive, how context is supplied, and how results return to the user. These questions can guide my reading and experiments after the event.
As a student, I find it helpful to break a problem into smaller steps, understand each component’s responsibility, and then connect the components. This approach should also help me explain my choices in my workshop report.
Learning and career direction The session gave me an opportunity to reflect on the skills I want to develop during my internship. Alongside AWS service knowledge, I want to improve at reading documentation, presenting ideas, and explaining technical decisions in terms of a practical need.
I also want to keep better learning notes, including what I tried, the results I observed, and the questions I still have. Those notes should help me communicate more clearly when seeking guidance from a mentor.
Key takeaways Start with a specific need. Before selecting technology, I should understand what a user wants to do and choose a manageable scope. Practice explaining a system. I want to understand how data moves, what each component does, and how to verify the result. Connect learning with a small product. A focused exercise can help me assess my understanding and identify gaps. Learn actively within the community. Attending in person gives me opportunities to encounter different perspectives and learning paths. Applying the learning during my internship After the event, I plan to choose a small problem, outline its workflow, and define its inputs and outputs before considering suitable AWS services. I will record my decisions, experiment results, and errors to support my worklog and personal workshop.
For AI topics, I want to study how context is provided with a request and how a bot’s answers can be evaluated. This is a direction for my further learning after the kickoff.
Event experience I attended as a listener, followed the presentations, and kept photos from the event. Visiting the AWS office, hearing the program introduction, and taking photos with others made this a memorable experience early in my internship.
The kickoff gave me more motivation to study Cloud and AI and think more concretely about the product I would like to build. The hands-on AI Agent Challenge listed in the published agenda did not take place during this event.
Event photos Figure 1. The opening session on September 26, 2026, featuring AWS First Cloud AI Journey.
Figure 2. My check-in photo beside the talkshow standee at the AWS office. The standee displays the topic, speaker, and event date.
Figure 3. A group photo with others at the event. All images in this article come from my personal event photo collection.
